answer: To enforce Sybil resistance, we parameterize a dynamic opportunity-cost bond ensuring the marginal cost of node creation exceeds Byzantine extraction. By mapping subgame-perfect slashing matrices to zero-knowledge verifiable delays, we prove identity multiplication yields strictly negative expected utility as the liquidation threshold acts as a jetty against erosion. Strict Nash equilibrium occurs when the summit of the staking curve renders the computational sonnet of adversarial coordination cost-prohibitive.
